title: Three Weeks and One Short Bandage
subtitle: 健康医疗 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 健康医疗（人与自我·生活与学习·健康的生活方式、个人安全与自救）
meta: 主题语境：健康医疗（人与自我·生活与学习·健康的生活方式、个人安全与自救）　|　核心词汇：ward　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 ward 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 the doctor ① visited the ward that no patient in the clinic would have recorded, and he said the visiting was the whole of the week. The ② ward, meaning the division itself and not the bandage, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; a ward, he said, is the only thing in a clinic that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ ward in that clinic had the same short bandage beside it, and the ④ ward at the far bed, meaning the scar they kept for the children to cover and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A ward, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the doctor said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the ward was the whole of the matter, meaning the care and not the division. The ⑥ ward, meaning the care and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; ward, he said, is either something you visit or the only word that means both a division and a care. He said the care is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ ward had become a line in a chart, and the chart had become an argument about the short bandage. The ⑧ ward of the whole thing, the doctor wrote in January, was one clinic and three weeks of recording; ward, he said, is either the scar at the far bed or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ ward I remember is the division recorded in the chart, which closed in 1971 and is still recorded as the quietest in the clinic. A ⑩ ward, my mother said in 1973, is the only division that improves by being recorded; every ward, she said, is a care that has agreed to look like a division. She said the care was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 病房；选区（指卫生所里每一间旁边的那一间）
B. n. 病房；选区（指那间病房本身，与窄窄的绷带相对）
C. 固定搭配：visit the ward 巡这一间病房
D. n. 病房；选区（指留给孩子们遮着的那一道）
E. n. 病房之事（抽象总称，指一处卫生所的病房之事）
F. n. 病房；选区（指病历里写到、被记载的那一间）
G. n. 病房、看护（指一件事里人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 看护（抽象总称，指人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: visited the ward that no patient in the clinic would have recorded
The ward, meaning the division itself and not the bandage
the ward at the far bed
the ward was the whole of the matter
the ward had become a line in a chart
The ward of the whole thing
A ward, my mother said in 1973

answers.why: visit the ward 意为“巡这一间病房”，1964 年那位大夫把卫生所里没有一位病人肯记载的一间病房做了一遍。
ward 意为“病房；选区”，指那间病房本身而不是窄窄的绷带，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记载。
ward 意为“病房；选区”，指卫生所里每一间旁边的那一间，每一间旁边都有同一卷窄窄的绷带。
ward 意为“病房；选区”，指最远那张床边的留给孩子们遮着的那一道，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
ward 意为“病房、看护”，指一件事里人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这间看护就是那件事的全部。
ward 意为“看护”，指人人都疼却无人提起的那样东西而不是那间病房，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
ward 意为“病房；选区”，指病历里写到、被记载的那一间，到 1969 年这一间成了病历里的一行。
ward 意为“病房之事”，大夫一月写道，整件事的病房之事是一处卫生所和三个星期的记载。
ward 意为“病房；选区”，我记得的是病历里记载过的那一间，1971 年养好了，至今仍被说成卫生所里最安静的一间。
ward 为抽象总称，母亲 1973 年说，病房是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的病房。
